title: Pressure
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Pressure Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Recall and apply density = mass ÷ volume; define pressure as force per unit area and apply p = F ÷ A; describe how pressure is transmitted in hydraulic systems such as a hydraulic press; recall and apply the relationship pressure due to a liquid column = height × density × g; describe how the height of a liquid column may be used to measure atmospheric pressure and how a manometer measures pressure differences (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on density and pressure: p = F/A, hydraulic jacks, pressure in liquids (p = hρg), atmospheric pressure, barometers and manometers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: In a liquid, p = hρg (g = 10 N/kg).
body_html:
How to think about it

Pressure is force per unit area.

  • p = F ÷ A in pascals (1 Pa = 1 N/m²). Change cm² into m² (1 m² = 10 000 cm²).
  • Density ρ = m ÷ V (kg/m³). An object floats in a liquid that is denser than it.
  • Pressure in a liquid p = hρg depends on depth and density, not on the shape of the container. Total pressure = atmospheric + hρg.
  • A hydraulic system passes the same pressure through the liquid: F₁ ÷ A₁ = F₂ ÷ A₂.
Example

Pressure of water at 4 m depth? (ρ = 1000 kg/m³)

p = 4 × 1000 × 10

Answer: 40 000 Pa

Example

A 600 N weight stands on 0.03 m². Pressure?

p = 600 ÷ 0.03

Answer: 20 000 Pa

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying force by area. Pressure = force ÷ area.
  • Using an area in cm² with an answer in Pa. Change it into m² first.
  • Thinking a wider container gives more pressure at the same depth.
  • Thinking a hydraulic system increases the pressure. It keeps the pressure the same and increases the force.

faq.q: What is the formula for pressure in a liquid?
faq.a: p = hρg: depth (m) × density (kg/m³) × gravitational field strength (10 N/kg). The answer is in pascals.

faq.q: How does a hydraulic jack work?
faq.a: A small force on a small piston makes a pressure that is passed through the liquid. The same pressure on a larger piston gives a larger force.
With a mercury barometer: atmospheric pressure holds up a column of mercury about 760 mm tall.

items.q: A mercury manometer shows a difference in levels of 30 cm, higher in the open arm. Atmospheric pressure is 100 000 Pa. What is the gas pressure? (density 13 600 kg/m³, g = 10 N/kg)
In a hydraulic jack, a force of 100 N acts on a small piston of area 0.01 m². The large piston has an area of 0.05 m². What force acts on the large piston?
items.e: Pressure is the same: F₂ = F₁ × A₂ ÷ A₁ = 100 × 5 = 500 N.

items.q: A force of 20 N on a piston of area 0.01 m² presses on oil in a hydraulic system. What is the pressure in the oil?

items.e: Δp = hρg = 0.15 × 13 600 × 10 = 20 400 Pa (use h in metres).
